fieldMarks: Very large, all-white swan with a massive all-black bill.
Lacks a yellow spot in front of the eye.
behavior: Bugling ko-hoh call, lower than the tundra swan's.
Feeds on submerged plants by reaching or up-ending; occasionally feeds on land in winter.
Southern populations are mostly non-migratory; northern birds move south in late fall as water freezes, flying low in V formations.
habitat: Large, shallow, vegetated freshwater ponds and wide, slow rivers; also lakes and winter bays.
range: Alaska, northwestern Canada and the northwestern US, with reintroduced populations in the Great Lakes region including Ontario, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan and Ohio.

lookalikes.name: Tundra swan
lookalikes.howToTell: Tundra swan is smaller, usually has a yellow spot before the eye and gives a higher call.
